excerpt: Tecton built a real-time feature platform for machine learning. Databricks agreed to acquire its assets in August 2025, and tecton.ai now redirects to Databricks.
content:
Tecton was a San Francisco company that built a feature platform, often called a feature store, for machine learning. A feature store turns raw data from databases, event streams and logs into the inputs (features) that models use, keeps a consistent history of them for training, and serves fresh values to models in production with low latency. Tecton's customers used it for real-time uses such as fraud detection, risk scoring and recommendations. Its founders, Mike Del Balso, Kevin Stumpf and Jeremy Hermann, had worked on machine learning infrastructure at Uber before starting the company in 2019.

Funding

Tecton raised about $160 million in total. Its last round, a $100 million Series C in 2022, was led by Kleiner Perkins with Databricks and Snowflake Ventures as strategic investors, alongside earlier backers Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital, according to AI Magazine. Verdict reported that the company had been valued at $900 million in that round and had about 90 employees.

Acquisition by Databricks

In August 2025 Databricks announced a deal to acquire Tecton. Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi told Reuters that Tecton's technology and team could strengthen Agent Bricks, Databricks' product for building AI agents, by feeding them real-time data. Financial terms were not disclosed. The law firm Fenwick, which advised Databricks, described the deal as an agreement to acquire the assets of Tecton. When we checked in October 2026, tecton.ai redirected to the Databricks website.

Pricing

Tecton no longer sells a standalone product with a public price list. Databricks prices its own platform separately.

What this means for users

Teams looking for Tecton-style real-time feature serving would now look at Databricks itself, or at independent options such as the open-source Feast project.

This page is based on reporting by Outlook Business (citing Reuters), Verdict, Techstrong.ai and AI Magazine, and on Fenwick's deal note.
